events.title: Mission San Diego de Alcalá Is Founded
events.description: Franciscan friar Junípero Serra founded Mission San Diego de Alcalá, the first of California's missions. It was the start of a chain of settlements along the Pacific coast.
events.significance: The mission grew into the city of San Diego. It also set the pattern for Spanish colonization in California, with lasting consequences for the region's Indigenous peoples.

events.title: The Residence Act Creates the U.S. Capital District
events.description: President George Washington signed the Residence Act. It authorized a permanent seat of government on the Potomac River.
events.significance: The act led to the creation of Washington, D.C. It settled a bitter early dispute over where the national capital would be.

events.title: The Trinity Test Ushers in the Atomic Age
events.description: In the New Mexico desert, the United States detonated a plutonium-based nuclear device. It was the first nuclear explosion ever conducted.
events.significance: The Manhattan Project's success changed warfare and global politics. It opened the nuclear era, and weeks later atomic bombs were used in Japan.

events.title: Apollo 11 Launches Toward the Moon
events.description: Apollo 11 lifted off from Cape Kennedy, Florida, carrying Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Michael Collins. It was bound for the first crewed Moon landing.
events.significance: Four days later, humans first walked on the Moon. The mission was a defining achievement of the Space Race.
